text:
Sanjay Patel: heads-up — I found a presigned s3 URL in staging service logs from a debug run. likely low-ttl but want a quick privacy/scope check before we escalate to legal/comms. INC-2026-0317-01
Maya Lee: can you paste the log line (redact bucket/path if needed) and confirm whether it appeared in hosted logs or local staging only? :eyes:
Sanjay Patel: pasted below (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z DEBUG request_id=abc123 user_id=redacted s3_url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/REDACTED/obj?X-Amz-Signature=... expires=2026-03-17T09:15:00Z
```
Sanjay Patel: it was from staging cluster in us-west-2, replayable via staging traffic only. not present in prod indexes as far as i can see.
Devon Chu: thanks. any PII in the object metadata or body?
Sanjay Patel: object was a small debug dump — no email/ssn in the blob according to quick grep. metadata had request_id and trace id only.
Maya Lee: ok — next Q: who has access to the staging logs? need list of teams and any external contractors.
Sanjay Patel: staging logs go to internal splunk index "staging-debug"; RBAC includes eng, eng-sre, support; contractors: none for that index AFAIK.
Maya Lee: good. given TTL was 3min and found in staging-only, risk looks low. recommended actions: 1) rotate any presigned creds if still valid (doesn't sound like it), 2) scrub log pipeline to strip presigned URLs at ingestion, 3) short comms note for ops channel confirming scope.
Priya (Product Comms): if you want a comms OK we need exact scope sentence — e.g., "staging-only, no customer data exposed, short-lived URL". i'll vet tone.
Devon Chu: i'll open a quick PR to a log-sanitizer rule: replace regex for presigned urls with "[REDACTED_S3_URL]" and run canary on staging. assigning to me.
Sanjay Patel: thanks Devon. can i get a thumbs-up on NOT doing a customer-facing notice? Maya?
Maya Lee: thumbs-up from security: no customer data, staging-only, short TTL. not a reportable breach. document in incident log and we're good. :white_check_mark:
ir-bot: Incident INC-2026-0317-01 created and tagged privacy-scope: low. Add owners: devon, sanjay, maya.
ops-bot: Notifying #eng-oncall for monitoring the sanitizer deploy tomorrow morning 09:00 UTC.
Priya (Product Comms): ok i'm on standby to approve internal comms. draft here when you have the language and i'll sign off.
Sanjay Patel: will draft a 2-line internal note and add to the incident ticket. thanks everyone. :pray:
Maya Lee: quick follow-up action: add a log ingestion scrub for presigned urls within 48h and a unit test so it doesn't regress. marking as action item in ticket.
Devon Chu: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/log-scrub/pull/472 — will canary deploy 09:00 UTC tomorrow.
Sanjay Patel: last check — any requests to rotate keys or to change IAM?
Maya Lee: no rotation necessary given short TTL and staging scope. if we find similar pattern in prod then we escalate.
Priya (Product Comms): approved internal comms language: "FYI — during a staging debug run a short-lived S3 presigned URL appeared in staging logs. No customer data was exposed. The engineering team sanitized logs and deployed a fix. No action required for customers."
Sanjay Patel: posting comms now and closing loop. thanks all. :tada:
